newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-WHITE SOX ROOKIES BLANK MARINERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-WHITE SOX ROOKIES BLANK MARINERS.

text.p: Rookies Scott Eyre and Keith Foulke combined on a four-hitter and Jorge Fabregas drove in three runs as the Chicago White Sox blanked the Seattle Mariners 5-0 on Monday.
In just his fourth major-league start, Eyre (2-2) pitched five innings, allowing three hits with three walks and four strikeouts.
Foulke allowed one hit, walked one and struck out four in four innings for his first major-league save as the White Sox gained a split of their four-game series with Seattle.
Seattle's best scoring chance came in the first inning when Alex Rodriguez and Edgar Martinez sandwiched a Ken Griffey double with walks to load the bases with one out.
But Eyre struck out Jay Buhner and Dan Wilson to leave the bases loaded.
"He was almost out of the game in the first inning with the bases loaded," said Chicago manager Terry Bevington. "If they get a couple of hits he's probably out of the game."
Fabregas had an RBI single to give the White Sox a 2-0 lead in the fourth and capped the scoring with a two-run single in the sixth.
Felipe Lira (5-8) allowed two runs and five hits in 3 2/3 innings in his first start since being acquired from the Detroit Tigers.

In Cleveland, Orel Hershiser allowed two earned runs in 5-2/3 innings to win his fourth straight decision and David Justice blasted a three-run homer in the first to lead the Indians to a 5-3 victory over the Toronto Blue Jays.
Hershiser (11-5) scattered three hits and three walks with one strikeout. Mike Jackson pitched 2 1/3 scoreless innings of relief before Jose Mesa worked a perfect ninth for the save.
Toronto starter Woody Williams (7-11) gave up five runs on eight hits over six innings to suffer the loss.
Justice's 24th homer of the season was his fifth round-tripper of the Indians' homestand. He hit .513 (20-for-39) and drove in 15 runs in just 11 games.

In Baltimore, pinch-hitter Harold Baines's sharp grounder to first in the bottom of the ninth inning scored Jeffrey Hammonds and lifted the Orioles a 2-1 victory over the Anaheim Angels and a sweep of their three-game series.

With Hammonds on third, Baines batted for Mike Bordick against left-hander Mike Holtz. On a 1-0 pitch, Baines hit a hard grounder next to the first-base bag that Darin Erstad knocked into foul territory, allowing Hammonds to score.

Erstad was charged with an error and Baines was credited with a game-winning RBI as Baltimore won for the 16th time in 21 games, extending its lead in the East to five games over the idle New York Yankees.
At Texas, the Rangers split a double header with the Milwaukee Brewers.
Julio Franco homered and scored three times and Gerald Williams drove in three runs as the Brewers won the opener 8-5.
Franco had three hits, including a solo homer in a the third. Williams added an RBI triple in the third as the Brewers jumped out to a 6-1 lead.
Juan Gonzalez hit his 29th and 30th homers for Texas.
Scott Karl (8-10) allowed four runs and eight hits in 5 1/3 innings for his sixth straight win. Tanyon Sturtze (1-1), who was tagged for six runs and six hits, was the loser.
In the nightcap, Rick Helling allowed just one hit over eight innings and Lee Stevens hit a pair of solo homers as the Rangers blanked the Brewers 2-0.
Helling (1-0), who pitched a perfect game in the minor leagues last year, pitched 5 2/3 innings of no-hit ball before Fernando Vina singled for Milwaukee's only hit of the game.
He walked two and struck out five in his first start for the Rangers since being re-acquired from the Florida Marlins last Sunday.
Stevens gave the Rangers all the offense they needed in the fifth when he blasted a 1-0 pitch from Joel Adamson (3-2) over the right-field wall for his 14th homer.
His second home run with two outs in the seventh inning provided Texas with an insurance run.
